plans.note: Only the preamble is exposed in the supplied outline, so no liability article can be pinned yet. A Master Services Agreement of this type almost always carries a limitation-of-liability clause; search the full text for 'Limitation of Liability', 'consequential', 'aggregate liability' and the fees-paid cap formula, then test for mutuality and for carve-outs (indemnities, confidentiality, IP infringement, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, data breach).

No indemnity section is visible in the outline provided. Before concluding it is missing, scan for 'indemnify', 'hold harmless', 'defend' and for third-party IP infringement language; if Kubient gives no indemnity, or if the only indemnity runs from AP as Customer, we add a Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity and keep any Customer indemnity narrow (AP-supplied content only).

Nothing in the visible outline suggests a covenant restricting AP's businesses or purchases. Confirm by searching 'non-compete', 'shall not engage', 'competing product/service' — including any restriction buried in an exclusivity, term or confidentiality clause — and only then treat as absent.

No exclusivity provision is discoverable from the preamble-only outline. Check for 'exclusive', 'sole provider', 'shall purchase solely from' and any 'preferred supplier' language in the services or term provisions; ad-tech MSAs sometimes hide exclusivity in inventory or channel commitments.

No pricing or MFN language appears in the supplied outline. Search 'most favoured/favored nation', 'no less favourable terms', 'best pricing' in the fees or pricing provisions; direction matters — an MFN in AP's favour is acceptable, one obliging AP to give Kubient its best terms is not.

Not visible in the outline. Look for 'solicit', 'hire', 'employ' near the confidentiality or general/miscellaneous provisions; if a non-solicit binds AP, it must be narrow, time-limited (12 months or less) and carry a general-advertising and unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

The preamble defines 'Initial Term', which signals a term-and-termination article elsewhere in the document. Locate that article and check whether AP has termination for convenience on reasonable notice (30-60 days) without penalty or early-termination fee, and whether Kubient has a reciprocal right we should strip or lengthen.

'Initial Term' is a defined term in the preamble, so a renewal mechanic is very likely in the term article. Verify any auto-renewal period, the non-renewal notice window (we want no more than 30 days for AP) and any uncapped price uplift on renewal.

Governing law and venue are standard in the miscellaneous provisions, which are not exposed in this outline. Confirm the chosen law is New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign or mandatory arbitration; note Kubient's offices in the preamble may drive the current choice.

Expect an assignment clause in the general provisions not shown here. Check that AP may assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger or asset sale without consent, and that Kubient cannot terminate or condition consent on AP's change of control; also confirm Kubient may not assign or subcontract without our consent.

An MSA with a media company will address IP and data ownership; that article is not surfaced in this outline. Search 'Intellectual Property', 'work product', 'deliverable', 'Customer Data', 'AP Content' and confirm AP retains ownership of its content, data and paid-for deliverables, with no assignment or broad licence-back to Kubient beyond what is needed to deliver the services.

Any platform or technology licence grant will sit in the services or licence article, not visible here. Check that AP's licence extends to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, and that it is not stated as 'revocable', 'at Licensor's discretion' or terminable at will.

No audit provision is visible from the preamble-only outline. Search 'audit', 'inspect', 'records', 'books' — if Kubient has audit rights over AP's usage, limit them to once per year, on prior written notice, during business hours, off-site where feasible, and at Kubient's cost absent material underpayment.

Not identifiable from the supplied outline. Check the fees, term and remedies provisions for 'liquidated damages', 'penalty', 'early termination fee' or 'shortfall payment' payable by AP; service credits running to AP are acceptable, damages running against AP are not.

Warranties and any disclaimer are not exposed in this outline. Search 'warrant', 'AS IS', 'DISCLAIMS ALL WARRANTIES' and confirm Kubient gives a workmanlike-performance and conformity warranty for a meaningful period with re-performance, repair or refund as the remedy; resist a bare 'AS IS' disclaimer.

No insurance article appears in the visible outline, which is a common gap in vendor-drafted MSAs. Confirm by searching 'insurance', 'coverage', 'certificate', 'additional insured'; because Kubient handles AP data, we should add commercial general liability, professional liability/E&O and cyber cover, with certificates on request.

Nothing in the outline reveals a volume commitment. Check the fees, order form or statement-of-work mechanics for 'minimum', 'committed spend', 'take-or-pay', 'shortfall'; any commitment binding AP needs an exit right or the ability to roll unused volume forward.

No survival or post-termination assistance language is visible. Search 'effect of termination', 'survival', 'return or destroy', 'transition' — if absent, we add a wind-down period, return of AP data in a usable format, certified deletion, and reasonable migration assistance at agreed rates.
